claims.scope: Tomczak and Godfrey report approximately 1,200 km from the Florida Straits along the coast to separation near Cape Hatteras. This is the Florida Current segment of the Gulf Stream System, not a whole-system length or a measured reference streamline. NOAA's glossary independently names the same segment; NASA and NOAA Coast Pilot sometimes use Gulf Stream more broadly for the Florida Straits flow.
claims.source_locator: Chapter 14, The Atlantic Ocean, PDF page 11 (printed page 239), paragraph beginning Recirculation of Gulf Stream water (1,200 km downstream to Cape Hatteras)

geometries.method: Approximate editorial locator points place a name in a recognizable region on the OSW equirectangular map. Points are neither observed cores nor endpoints or length measurements. Multi-basin family names have one point per basin and must be split into separate records before quantitative comparison.
geometries.positional_uncertainty: not quantified; no observed current core or path
